reviews.title: Amazing Value—Performs Like Grinders Costing 5x More
reviews.body: I don’t usually leave reviews, but this hand grinder impressed me enough that I felt it deserved one.For the price, this grinder is fantastic. I’ve used hand grinders that cost $150 or more, and honestly, I can’t taste or see much of a difference between those and this one. Maybe experienced coffee experts can, but for the average to intermediate coffee enthusiast, this grinder performs exceptionally well.The build quality feels solid, it produces a consistent grind, and the larger capacity is a nice bonus if you’re brewing multiple cups at once.My only minor regret is choosing the 60g version. I typically grind about 30g per day, split between two brews, so I don’t really need the extra capacity. That said, the larger size isn’t a dealbreaker, and considering the price, it’s an incredible value.One major tip: Before grinding, add 2–3 small drops of water to the beans in the chamber. Don’t overdo it—you only need a couple of drops. This dramatically reduces static electricity, which means far less mess and fewer coffee grounds sticking everywhere. You’ll thank me later.Overall, if you’re looking for an affordable hand grinder that delivers performance well above its price point, I highly recommend this one.

reviews.title: I really like this grinder!
reviews.body: I’m really impressed with this grinder. It’s a great price, compact, and easy to use. I was hesitant to order it because it had relatively few reviews compared to some of the bigger name brands, but I am pleasantly surprised with it’s quality.I’ve had a hand grinder in the past, but I did not like the grind quality and it was a chore to use. This one is easy to adjust, and quick and easy to grind. It’s also much quieter than an electric grinder.I use an AeroPress, and I only make coffee for myself. If I was regularly making a large batch of ground coffee this would not be my go-to tool. For one to two people brewing coffee on demand this grinder is perfect.I travel a few times a year for work and have resorted to instant or preground coffee because anything is better than the hotel coffee packets. I had been wanting to find a better solution, and now I find myself looking forward to my next trip. This handy little grinder is going to greatly increase the joy of travelling.A couple of things to note. The outside black shell is plastic, the crank shaft that holds the burr appears to be stainless steel along with the burr. The clear cup that catches the grounds, is glass. Some of the older reviews show an orange glass, but the newer one is clear.Some other hand grinders advertise being able to use a hand drill. The crank shaft is the correct shape, but it appears an odd size. A 7/32in socket fits and works well enough, but it has a little more play than usual. I think a 5.5mm socket might fit better, but I don’t have one to try. You can also use the chuck directly on the shaft. I was looking forward to using a drill to speed things up, but I found that I enjoyed grinding by hand enough that I only used the drill once.

reviews.title: More time
reviews.body: My first burr grinder. Picked it because of the stainless steel burrs. Maybe save some $ because its manually powered vs an electric one. First off I really like the consistant grind my coffee tastes even better. But I had to get used to the time it takes to grind. So if I'm cranking at about 50-60 rpm on setting 22 it takes roughly 180 turns to grind a full load.About 3 minutes. I noticed if I grind slower it processes more beans per crank but has more resistance.The finer the grind.the more turns required. So I like it. It holds the exact amount of beans I require and is versatile for use anywhere anytime. I just had to get used to the prep time.I almost benched it after the first use but find it worth the effort.The action is smooth ,there are 2 sealed bearings and it does feel like quality although mostly made of plastic. I dropped it and cracked the selector ring. Was able to repair with a hot staple. I paid around 30 which is ok in comparison,. Should last a while if I don't drop it anymore.

reviews.title: Excellent value, good grind quality
reviews.body: This hand grinder contradicts "buy cheap, get cheap' dictum. Expected a stop gap temporary fill in unit I got a new higher end machine. This one works so well, I decided to delay spending more money. It is everything it claimed. So far has given me consistent grinds for press to Espresso. Takes a bit of elbow grease for finer grinds and some experimenting to dial in the size.The grind settings viewable outside and the rubber ring makes for a convenient non slip grip while grinding. Not a 5 Star because of high static and a bit of a choice to get the retention out. My usual go to anti static trick of wiping down the plastic container periodically with a dab of alcohol seems to do the trick.

reviews.title: Best Grinder Out There
reviews.body: I absolutely LOVE this coffee grinder.  I've had an electric one for years now, and this grinder puts that thing to shame.To start, the precision of the coarse grind is perfect for cold brew coffee, which is what I prefer for the higher caffeine content.  Two full grinds in this is exactly the right amount needed for my cold brew jar.  I've only made two jars of cold brew thus far, so four full grinds, and it has not flinched once.Using the grinder is as simple as screwing the catch jar on the bottom, filling it with beans, placing the handle on top, and turning.  It's compact enough to fit easily into a suitcase or backpack to use wherever you may go.The one drawback is that you do have to be careful while grinding to make sure handle and lid do not come off.  It only slides into place and is not securely attached.  This only happened to me once, and it was because I was admittedly being a bit careless.  Nonetheless, it is something to be aware of.If you enjoy a particular style of coffee and want to make sure you get EXACTLY the best grind for your particular taste, then this is the grinder for you.  You will not regret it.

reviews.title: Fantastic, far exceeded my expectations!
reviews.body: Ive used it for over a month and can say im actually quite surprised by the grind quality. I was using an eletric blade grinder before and didnt realize I could change the flavor of my coffee based on grind size. I really like how adjustable it is and how quickly you can grind a good bit of coffee beans. Its easy to clean and is also nice looking so it looks good in the kitchen around my other coffee stuff when guests are over. Overall I'd buy this again and again and again.
